h1: Just Better Painting vs. Precision Paint Experts
heroIntro: Two exterior bids on the same house rarely describe the same job. Here is a practical way to lay them next to each other and see what each one actually covers.

sections.h2: Start with the job, not the bottom line
body: If Just Better Painting's proposal is on your kitchen table next to ours, this page is for you. It won't characterize anybody else's work. What it does offer is a method: a way to put any two exterior quotes on the table and find out whether they are pricing the same house.

The grand total is the number on a bid that tells you the least. Before you compare totals, make sure both proposals describe the same surfaces, the same preparation, and the same coating system. If one quote covers the fascia, soffits, and garage door and the other does not, the cheaper one is simply a smaller job.

sections.h2: A line-by-line worksheet for exterior quotes
body: Draw two columns and fill in each row from the paperwork, not from the sales conversation. Anything you cannot find in writing gets a question mark.
bullets: Surfaces included and excluded: siding, trim, doors, shutters, soffits, gutters, railings, porch ceilings.
Washing method and whether mildew treatment is part of it.
Scraping, sanding, new caulk, and primer on bare spots: written out, or just implied?
Rotted wood and fascia: who finds it, and how the fix gets approved.
The named primer, the named finish coat, and how many coats of each.
Start window, expected working days, and dry time.
Warranty length and what it covers, in writing.

sections.h2: How our estimate fills in those rows
body: With us, the house is walked by a Precision Paint Experts crew lead rather than someone on commission. They take measurements and photos and run moisture checks wherever siding or trim looks questionable. Within a business day or so, the written, itemized estimate lands in your inbox.

Each line of that worksheet gets filled in by our quote: which surfaces are covered and which aren't, every prep task, the primer and finish product line, how many coats, and when the work happens. Two full coats is standard; a third goes on for a bold color switch or a surface that soaks up paint, and wherever spraying alone won't drive the coating in, a painter back-brushes or back-rolls it. Nothing is added later without your written approval.

sections.h2: The rows that usually explain a price gap
body: When two bids differ sharply, look first at the prep rows. A proper wash and mildew treatment, fresh caulk, and primer on bare spots eat up real crew hours, and they determine how many years the paint survives Florida weather. Our article on how long exterior paint lasts in Florida explains the connection.

Product is the second row to check. Our bids specify premium Sherwin-Williams or Benjamin Moore: 100% acrylic for siding and trim, and elastomeric wherever stucco shows hairline movement. Because the exact line is printed on the quote, you can pull up its data sheet and judge it for yourself.

sections.h2: Put a written bid next to the one you have
body: If you already hold a quote, a second written scope makes the worksheet easy to finish. We don't charge for estimates or expect a commitment, a crew lead can usually be at your house within 48 hours, and most exterior painting jobs get underway one to three weeks after you sign. Exterior work is backed by our written workmanship warranty, good for up to 10 years and stacked on the manufacturer's product warranty. Request your free estimate and line the two scopes up side by side.

faqs.q: Is it fair to ask a painter to break out prep work separately?
faqs.a: Yes. Most of a painting crew's hours go into prep, so asking any contractor to itemize it is entirely fair. Ours spells out washing, scraping, sanding, caulking, repairs, and spot-priming in the written scope.

faqs.q: What if two quotes name different paint brands?
faqs.a: Compare the specific product lines and coat counts rather than the brand names alone. Our quote prints the exact product from Sherwin-Williams or Benjamin Moore, so you can read its spec sheet.

faqs.q: How many days should an exterior repaint take?
faqs.a: Count on three to seven working days for the painting, then add the wash and the drying time. You'll see the timeline in writing on our quote.
